author: Bobby Grayson
description:
CLOSED (gone from the readiness families): if/case not at body level 98, pipe 38, block as a sub-expression 26, variable binding x = e 20, binding a pattern x = e 16, operator && 12, operator || 10, operator in 9, cond 3, operator * 2, if/case after a statement with an effect 9. Kernel function or guard 33 -> 28; the 28 left are put_in/get_in/update_in (Access), is_reference/is_port, inspect/to_string/binary_part/byte_size (strings) and ceil (floats), none of them mine.
NEW, NARROWER KINDS that name what is genuinely still unsupported: "a statement with an effect inside a block expression" 16, "if/case as a statement (its value is discarded)" 23, "binding a pattern that may not match" 5.
SHARP EDGE not fixed: case over a comparison, e.g. case x > 10 do true -> ..; false -> .. end, emits match (x > 10) with | true => .., and Lean cannot match a Prop against true/false (expr renders == as = and and/or as the Prop connectives). Pre-existing, not introduced here, but the expression compiler makes it reachable in more places. The fix is a decide (..) wrapper on a Bool-typed case scrutinee whose AST is a comparison or a boolean connective.
DELIBERATE: is_binary/1 is implemented as a clear error and is NOT on the readiness allowlist, because the model has no binaries at all. If wf7/stdlib adds a string type it should make is_binary decide on it and add it there. Likewise div/rem are Nat only, because Elixir div truncates toward zero and Lean integer division does not.
Ensemble.LogStore is now blocker-free in the walker; its remaining translator failure is name: Keyword.get(opts, :name, __MODULE__) as a registered name, which is wf7/stdlib or wf7/locals territory.
title: wf7/control: what closed, what is left, and the sharp edges
